# libphonenumber-csharp

> C# port of Google's libphonenumber: parse, format and validate international phone numbers.
> Two NuGet packages: libphonenumber-csharp (the port, mirrors Google's Java API) and
> libphonenumber-csharp.extensions (C#-idiomatic helpers: TryParse, formatting extension methods,
> System.Text.Json converter, DataAnnotations attribute). Both target netstandard2.0, net8.0 and
> net10.0 and are trim/Native AOT compatible.

## Correct usage

- Import `using PhoneNumbers;` only. Do NOT import `PhoneNumbers.Extensions`: it is the obsolete
  first version of the extensions package (warnings PNX0001-PNX0005), and its static class
  `PhoneNumbers.Extensions.PhoneNumber` collides with the core type `PhoneNumbers.PhoneNumber`.
- Core (no extensions package): `var util = PhoneNumberUtil.GetInstance();`
  `PhoneNumber n = util.Parse("020 7031 3000", "GB");` (throws `NumberParseException`),
  `util.Format(n, PhoneNumberFormat.E164)`, `util.IsValidNumber(n)`, `util.GetNumberType(n)`.
  Enum members are SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE as in Java: `PhoneNumberFormat.E164`,
  `PhoneNumberType.FIXED_LINE`.
- Non-throwing parse (extensions package): `if (PhoneNumber.TryParse(s, "GB", out PhoneNumber? n))`
  on C# 14+; `PhoneNumberParser.TryParse(s, "GB", out PhoneNumber? n)` on C# 13 or earlier and VB.
  `TryParseValid` additionally requires a valid number. The region is a two-letter CLDR code;
  omit it (or pass null) to accept international format ("+44...") only.
- Formatting (extensions package): `n.Format(PhoneNumberFormat.E164)`, `n.IsValidNumber()`,
  `n.GetNumberType()`, `n.GetRegionCodeForNumber()`.
- JSON (extensions package): `using PhoneNumbers.Text.Json;`
  `new JsonSerializerOptions().AddPhoneNumberConverter()`. Native AOT: put
  `[JsonSourceGenerationOptions(Converters = new[] { typeof(PhoneNumberJsonConverter) })]` on your
  own JsonSerializerContext. Never serialize a PhoneNumber without the converter.
- Validation attribute (extensions package): `using PhoneNumbers.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations;`
  `[ValidPhoneNumber(DefaultRegion = "GB")]` on a string or PhoneNumber property.
- ASP.NET Core route/query parameters of type PhoneNumber and IOptions<T> properties of type
  PhoneNumber bind with no setup, in international format only. For national input bind a string
  and call TryParse with the region.
- Never write a custom TypeConverter for PhoneNumber or register `PhoneNumberTypeConverter`; the
  core type has one built in.
- `PhoneNumber.ToString()` is a debug dump ("Country Code: 44 National Number: 2070313000"), not a
  format. Use Format.
